extracted.intended_audience: Reuters journalists and editorial staff worldwide
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and ethical standards that govern reporting, visual journalism and related activities at Reuters, covering accuracy, sourcing, independence, conflicts of interest, use of AI, and conduct both on and off duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the Trust Principles in all activities related to Reuters News
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the Trust Principles in all activities related to Reuters News.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Trust Principles underpin all Reuters journalism; decisions should protect Reuters’ independence, integrity and impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold accuracy sacrosanct
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold accuracy sacrosanct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy is at the heart of what we do — it is better to be late than wrong; accuracy and balance always take precedence over speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek fair comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek fair comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give subjects the opportunity to put their side; ensure opinions quoted are authoritative and attributed; avoid misrepresenting views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct errors transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct errors transparently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rectify errors promptly, clearly and comprehensively in stories, captions, graphics or scripts; be transparent about corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strive for balance and freedom from bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive for balance and freedom from bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be scrupulously fair and balanced; avoid language that implies judgement; reflect all relevant sides of an issue without taking sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose potential or actual conflicts of interest to a manager
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose potential or actual conflicts of interest to a manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any activity could raise a perception of bias or conflict, raise it with your manager; disclosure is required for personal investments, relationships, outside work, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid injecting unattributed opinion in a news story
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid injecting unattributed opinion in a news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News must be fact-based; opinions belong in clearly labelled columns or services; quoted opinion must be attributed to a named source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not fabricate or plagiarise
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not fabricate or plagiarise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never invent facts, quotes or sources; always attribute material that is not original to its source to avoid plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not alter still images or video footage beyond normal editorial preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not alter still images or video footage beyond the methods normally used to prepare content for editorial use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual journalism must reflect unaltered reality; avoid any manipulations that add to or detract from the reality portrayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pay for information or accept a bribe or trade on privileged information
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not pay for information or accept a bribe or trade on privileged information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No payments, gifts or benefits may be used to influence reporting; facilitation payments are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy is at the heart of what we do. It is our job to get it first but it is above all our job to get it right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always prioritise accuracy and balance over speed; think how you would withstand a challenge or denial before publishing; cross-check information whenever possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters is transparent about errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rectify mistakes promptly, clearly and comprehensively across all formats (story, caption, graphic, script); processes for corrections should be followed without delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy entails honesty in sourcing and the credibility of sources underpins Reuters’ reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use named sources where possible and press them to go on the record; use unnamed sources only when necessary for market or public interest and assume responsibility for accuracy; make ground rules clear with sources, take notes and record where allowed; cross-check information and talk to all sides; publish single-anonymous-source stories only in exceptional cases subject to special authorisation; protect source confidentiality but be prepared to disclose to supervisors on legitimate editorial grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes are sacrosanct and must not be altered other than to delete a redundant word or clause without changing sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selective quoting can unbalance a story — ensure quotes are representative; provide context and body language where relevant; consult senior colleagues if unsure about running a verbatim quote; minor grammatical corrections may be valid but do not reword entire phrases; translate idiomatically to preserve tone and meaning; prefer reported speech when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflecting reality
rubrics_metrics.description: Images and stories must reflect reality; avoid hyping or sensationalising material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid language and visual practices that mislead (e.g., ‘flood’ when numbers are small); no visual actions that add to/detract from reality; manipulations that constitute fabrication can lead to disciplinary measures including dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datelines and bylines
rubrics_metrics.description: Use datelines and bylines accurately — readers assume the byline shows the writer was at the dateline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Byline only where the writer or reporter being written up on a desk was present; use datelines only when staff/freelancers on the spot are providing information; include contributors in an additional-reporting line with name and location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide proper attribution to the source of material that is not ours in stories, photographs or moving images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label sources specifically (e.g., 'Greenpeace Video' rather than 'handout'); clearly attribute material gathered by others including rival organisations to avoid plagiarism and to allow assessment of reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting rumours
rubrics_metrics.description: Report facts, not rumours; distinguish clearly between fact and rumour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When rumours affect markets, attempt to verify or knock them down; only in exceptional circumstances (e.g., rapid, violent market moves) may a story move before full verification, and such cases require caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic images and obscenities
rubrics_metrics.description: Convey reality accurately but avoid gratuitous publication of graphic images, details or obscene language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There must be a valid news reason to run graphic material and usually a senior editor decision; consider audience and market thresholds; packaged videos must carry 'Warning: Graphic Content' and RAW videos require warnings in scripts/slates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence is essential: Reuters must be 'stateless' and report without regard to outside commercial or political interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflicts of interest or perceptions thereof; raise any potential conflicts with your manager; editorial decisions must be based only on accuracy, balance and truth, not commercial considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Investments
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not allow personal or immediate family investments to influence your work for Reuters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must not report on or edit stories about entities in which you or immediate family have an interest; do not trade on information that could create a conflict; follow Thomson Reuters Code of Conduct and local disciplinary procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring financial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare financial interests to avoid any suspicion of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Thomson Reuters Code of Conduct for requirements on personal investments and access to non-public information; failure to adhere may lead to disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work outside Reuters
rubrics_metrics.description: Paid work outside Reuters requires prior permission from your manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include books, articles, conference speaking or commercial photography; permission is routinely granted if activities do not affect Reuters; NewsGuild members in the US only need permission if the second job could compete with Reuters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking back with sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit stories to sources for vetting; you may check back to verify quotes or facts but avoid giving sources chance to materially alter content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist requests from interview subjects to pre-approve quotes; if quotes must be submitted for approval, do not agree to material changes; checking is for verification, not vetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts and entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept payments, gifts, services or benefits from news sources or contacts that could influence reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept nominal traditional gifts only with caution; gifts of more than nominal value should be declined or surrendered to a manager; hospitality acceptable only if newsworthy and reasonable; never accept junkets or entertainment without news value; consult manager when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and accommodation provided by sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters normally pays its own way; free travel or accommodation from sources is generally not accepted without manager approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission may be granted in exceptional cases where access otherwise impossible (e.g., remote famine, military flights); obtain manager approval and try to reimburse the provider when practical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bribes and other inducements
rubrics_metrics.description: Never take or offer payment for a news story; avoid offering anything that could constitute an improper benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such acts are a grave breach of ethics and grounds for dismissal; be aware of local legal restrictions on what officials may accept; Reuters forbids facilitation payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence within Reuters
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain editorial independence from Reuters’ business/commercial units and from external commercial interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not alter coverage to aid sales contracts or commercial interests; consider reasoned editorial complaints from non-editorial colleagues but examine them on merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering competitions and receiving awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit work for awards only with managerial approval and only to reputable, disinterested contests judged by journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not produce Reuters work primarily for awards or alter work except to meet contest rules; some contests or awards (corporate, political, advocacy) require senior approval; unsolicited awards and jury invitations need approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to the highest ethical standards and the Thomson Reuters Trust Principles at all times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept responsibilities, act with personal integrity, respect local laws and cultures, and avoid actions that could damage Reuters’ reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying ourselves as journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not obtain news by deception or pass yourself off as anything other than a journalist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only in exceptional circumstances where an assumption is allowed for newsgathering should identity be ambiguous; if directly questioned, always identify as a Reuters journalist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting from the Internet
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the same standards of sourcing, identification and verification online as in other forms of newsgathering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take precautions online, verify provenance, and do not use material that cannot be sourced and verified; treat internet-origin content with same scrutiny as other sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insider trading
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not participate in insider trading or tipping based on material non-public information obtained through Reuters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information is material if likely to affect a security’s price; assume information obtained in employment is non-public; tipping and trading on such information are prohibited and can be criminal offences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate sources professionally, maintain detachment, and avoid relationships that could create bias or the appearance of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be polite and fair; do not spend excessive leisure time with sources; disclose romantic or family attachments to a manager; do not report on or quote family members to avoid favouritism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with customers
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a clear line between editorial activity and commercial/customer relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not negotiate sales contracts or engage in commercial dealings with customers; discuss editorial issues but avoid mixing editorial and commercial roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with people (sensitivity in coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat people in the news with sensitivity and avoid unnecessary harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat victims with sensitivity, avoid needless pain and offence, seek clear unambiguous facts, avoid sensationalism and hype, be alert for spin and other manipulation, and be wary of assumptions and personal bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with competitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Compete vigorously but ethically with other news organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain information about competitors responsibly; acknowledge their exclusive reporting; do not do deals or trade material with competitors; cooperate when justified for safety or mutual interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate and respond promptly and properly to complaints about accuracy, balance or ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge complaints quickly, investigate promptly, handle at a senior level if needed, escalate to Ethics and Standards when in doubt; maintain constructive attitude and avoid hostility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with the authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer requests from police, tribunals or other authorities for published or unpublished Reuters content to a senior editor and legal team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish published from unpublished material; do not voluntarily hand over unpublished material; consider lawful challenges to orders or subpoenas to protect staff safety and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with each other
rubrics_metrics.description: Foster teamwork, mutual respect and a workplace free from harassment, intimidation or offensive behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share information, ideas and the burden of coverage; staff should feel able to raise standards or ethics concerns without fear of recrimination; treat colleagues and applicants with dignity and respect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Report serious incidents that affect staff safety, stories/images, hoaxes or allegations of improper behaviour to supervisors promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers must be informed quickly so senior officials remain aware of events that could embarrass or harm Reuters; spotting trends across regions is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life outside Reuters
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid blurring professional activities with private interests; follow the Thomson Reuters Code of Conduct in outside activities and use of company systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not express political opinions or investment advice on company systems in ways that identify Reuters with a cause; use private email for personal matters and avoid using Reuters identity to obtain personal benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain Reuters’ neutrality: park nationality and politics at the door and seek balanced reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive to be scrupulously fair and balanced; avoid portraying allegations as fact; give subjects opportunity to respond; watch word choice to avoid implying judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take no side, tell all sides
rubrics_metrics.description: Never identify with any side in an issue, conflict or dispute; reflect all relevant sides in text and visual stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectivity does not always mean equal space — editorial judgement determines weight; always ask 'What do I know?' and 'What do I need to know?' and ensure fairness to subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinion and Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish clearly between fact-based news and labelled opinion pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not express personal opinions in news stories, voiced video, scripts or work-related blogs; opinion pieces must be clearly labelled and carry disclaimers that they do not represent Reuters; columns should be grounded in expertise, not ungrounded provocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminatory language and stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid inappropriate references and unconscious stereotyping in descriptions of people and groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use neutral language; include characteristic details only when relevant and handled sensitively; prefer gender-neutral plurals for professional groups; be cautious with country stereotypes and dated assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not express personal investment views in reports; any value judgments on investments must be sourced to a named third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reuters reports news, not investment advice; local laws may prohibit giving investment advice; avoid advising customers or readers in any channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on Thomson Reuters
rubrics_metrics.description: Take extreme care to avoid bias when reporting on Thomson Reuters and its affiliates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories about Thomson Reuters must be seen before publication by senior regional editors and the Global Editor for Ethics and Standards; include comment from a company spokesman and follow policies on market-moving pickups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political and Community Activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not give support to political parties or identify Reuters with any political group; be sensitive to outside activity that may create a perception of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use common sense, the Trust Principles and consult managers when in doubt; staff may be required to move duties if outside activity creates perceptions of conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal Opportunity in the Newsroom
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat employees fairly regardless of gender, ethnicity, religion, age, disability, marital or parental status, sexual orientation or other protected characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hiring, training, promotion and selection should be based solely on skills, abilities and job-relevant requirements, in accordance with local laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity in the Newsroom
rubrics_metrics.description: Embrace diversity of thought, style, experience, culture, race, gender identity and other differences to enrich journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Welcome varying perspectives as they contribute to better reporting and debate about the news we gather.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media interviews and speaking engagements (approval and conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews and speaking engagements must be approved and conducted in a way that does not compromise Reuters’ objectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews require manager and communications team approval; Reuters services take precedence; requests must come from credible outlets; correspondents should not give personal opinions or seek/accept payment; inadvertent payments must be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference participation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in conferences requires editorial approval and must not undermine Reuters’ independence or create perceptions of influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval needed for events sponsored by companies; journalists should moderate only with full editorial control; avoid panels where participants paid to attend or where purpose is to launch/sell a product; editors limited to one appearance a year at a company's conference; reporters covering a company should not participate in that company's events; do not seek or accept payment or expenses except in limited TR-approved circumstances; press coverage is editorial decision, not a condition of participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artificial Intelligence and Generative AI (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Embrace AI opportunities but maintain editorial accountability and transparency about use of GenAI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all AI-assisted output is verified and fact-checked; be transparent about GenAI use; seek guidance from Ethics and Standards and Legal when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI and visual journalism (prohibition on AI-generated visuals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use generative AI to create or enhance any imagery; visual journalism must present unaltered reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI may assist tasks that do not alter underlying visuals (e.g., describing a scene or generating shotlists/captions). Any AI-generated or AI-modified visual elements are strictly prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of third-party tools and data protection with AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not upload Reuters, partner or third-party content to non-approved external tools, including free tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only explicitly authorised tools and use cases may be used; these restrictions protect authenticity, verifiability and intellectual property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat AI-generated material with scepticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Never trust or use unverified, unattributed facts generated by AI systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LLMs can sound persuasive but may lack nuance and reflect biases; independently verify all facts, sources and claims produced by AI and subject them to usual impartiality checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial accountability for AI outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters and individual journalists remain responsible for content produced with AI assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists are accountable for all work regardless of tools used; verify and fact-check AI output and consult Ethics & Standards or Legal when uncertain.
